linesVerbatim: ## Common component developer and operability contract
Language analyzers and tools do not reimplement cross-cutting product behavior.
The host plus common component SDK/control contract provides standardized:
- structured candidate/result/fault envelopes and host-owned human, JSON, and
- diagnostic taxonomy, redaction, bounds, structured logging/audit correlation,
- schema-checked configuration with provenance and brokered secret handles;
- artifact/state brokers, cancellation, deadlines, resource reporting, trust,
Components may emit domain candidates, events, progress, and bounded structured
diagnostics. They must not render product UI directly, choose verdicts/exits,
seal evidence, write unstructured host logs, or bypass host brokers. Common
look-and-feel and operability across components are DR-125/DR-G20 acceptance
properties; exact SDK APIs and frameworks remain implementation design.

governingSources.role: T-1 tension text as reported by the adopted CPC. This artifact proposes the composition. It does not rewrite DR-102.

INHERITED v1-era pin. Named properties only: D-007 capability-declaration dual boundary; D-002 slice-affecting. D-015 adopted control-protocol-contract.v2, which reported T-1. D-015 did not route a reserved disposition to DR-125. Live digest at reMeasurementAtV2.
Live DR-125 row. The cancellation/doctor/exit integration fragment lives on this row, not as a D-015 routing grant.

standardizedFamilies.name: envelopes and host-owned projections
standardizedFamilies.rule: Components emit domain candidates/results/faults. Human/JSON/SARIF projections are host-owned. SARIF advertisement follows the DR-122 contract (preview: none advertised).

standardizedFamilies.name: diagnostics, redaction, logs, progress
standardizedFamilies.rule: Bounded structured diagnostics only. No unstructured host logs. Redaction is host-owned.

standardizedFamilies.name: schema-checked configuration and secret handles
standardizedFamilies.rule: Configuration is namespaced and schema-checked. Secret values are brokered handles. Handle storage is DR-108 (deferred).

standardizedFamilies.name: brokers, cancellation, deadlines, resources, trust, lifecycle, doctor
standardizedFamilies.rule: Components use host brokers. They do not open raw host resources. Doctor integration consumes DR-114; it does not mint doctor schema.

standardizedFamilies.name: verdict/finalization/D9/exit mapping
standardizedFamilies.rule: The host maps. Components never choose verdicts, exits, or sealed termination. D9 values are DR-007's.

capabilityDeclarationSurface.rule: The host owns the capability vocabulary that bounds the DR-118 matrix (D-007 OBS-T2-02). Manifest capabilities[] are data over that vocabulary, not a self-granted contract.
capabilityDeclarationSurface.doesNotMint: This artifact does not mint the capability token list. It states the ownership: host-contract declaration is the boundary; the manifest cannot add a capability the host has not registered.

t1CancellationComposition.standing: PROPOSED composition. Not a self-granted conversion of a coordinator-reserved disposition. Not a claim that D-015 routed the decision here.
t1CancellationComposition.provenance: D-015 adopted control-protocol-contract.v2, which reported the T-1 tension. File 08 DR-125 acceptance cell names cancellation integration. This row proposes the composition those two facts leave open.

split.controlPlaneCancel: SUPERVISION-SCOPED teardown announcement. It is not an in-band data-plane message and never becomes one.
split.providerInBandCancel: Wholly owned by the host's provider-side participant under the applied provider contract. The control plane MUST NOT inject, wrap, translate, or author that Cancel frame.

hostEventTransitionRelation.sampleEligibilityAt: Immediately before any CPC teardown action that could preclude an in-band Cancel, against the applied provider contract's admissible causes and current state.
hostEventTransitionRelation.ifAdmissible: Commit the provider-side in-band Cancel transition FIRST. Then emit CPC supervision teardown. Neither authors the other's frame.
hostEventTransitionRelation.ifNotAdmissible: Emit only CPC supervision teardown. Do not invent a provider Cancel.

dualCarrierFanoutRequiredWhen: host-initiated cancellation whose cause the applied provider contract currently admits as in-band Cancel
deadline expiry owned by the host, likewise only if currently admissible
composition.onHostObservedProcessDeath: The control plane appends the death boundary event and runs the teardown ladder. No in-band Cancel is sent: the provider transition is unavailable from a terminal state. The phrase cancellation-equivalent is not used.
composition.noFanoutWhen: A provider-side in-band Cancel with no independently host-owned control-cancellation event remains wholly within the provider contract and never creates CPC supervision meaning.
composition.j1: J-1 appends independently emitted events to the merged order. The owning contract alone assigns meaning. J-1 does not grant the control plane a translation exception.
composition.mustNot: The control plane cannot translate provider meaning to resolve a race (file 02). No exception.

t1CancellationComposition.join: J-1 binds ordering only. Fate/D9/exit remain host-owned under the owning contracts.
alternativesRejected: Control plane authors provider Cancel frames — rejected: translates provider meaning.
Drop in-band Cancel — rejected: starves the applied provider contract's closed host-to-worker set.
Claim D-015 already decided the composition — rejected: D-015 adopted the CPC report, not a DR-125 grant.

g20.executes: Look-and-feel and operability goldens; forbidden-act negatives; T-1 composition goldens (supervision cancel vs in-band Cancel; no control-plane-authored provider Cancel).
g20.doesNotClaim: QUALIFIED. Exact SDK APIs remain implementation design.

reserved: argument-vector policy token list (already reserved from DR-105)
